question: Which of the following types of engine classifications is based on cylinder arrangement?
solution:
The correct answer is __V-engine.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Engine classifications based on cylinder arrangement__ include configurations such as inline engines, V-engines, and flat engines.
 
• A V-engine has cylinders arranged in two banks set at an angle to each other, forming a "V" shape.
 
• V-engines are known for their compact size and ability to deliver higher power outputs compared to inline engines.
 
• This design helps in reducing engine length and lowering the center of gravity, improving vehicle stability.
 
• Common examples of V-engines include V6, V8, and V12 engines.
 
• They are widely used in high-performance and luxury vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Inline Engine:**

 
 
• Cylinders are arranged in a single straight line, either vertically or horizontally.
 
• It is simpler in design and widely used in compact vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Flat Engine:**
 
 
• Also known as a boxer engine, its cylinders lie flat and horizontally opposed to each other.
 
• This arrangement helps in achieving a lower center of gravity.
 
 
 
• **Radial Engine:**
 
 
• Commonly used in aircraft, the cylinders are arranged radially around a central crankshaft.
 
• It provides high power-to-weight ratio.
